overall.sentence: An antidot that selects which localized anyon the interfering e/2 quasiparticle braids around, giving pi and pi/2 jumps at half filling, is new in bilayer graphene, but GaAs work at 5/2 (Willett et al., uncited) already reported e/4 and e/2 braiding signatures with pi phase flips, and the GaAs antidot interferometer of Ref. 19 already set up the method; the arXiv API failed, so this grade rests on the references and five web searches only.

assessment.claim: 1: gate-tunable FPI in bilayer graphene with an embedded antidot gives local control over the number and type of localized anyons
assessment.note: Ref. 19 (Ghosh et al., GaAs) already embedded an antidot in an FPI to act on anyons; question and method match, the system (bilayer graphene, even-denominator) is new. A concurrent graphene antidot paper (arXiv:2603.11182) was posted the same day, after this one. Weak search: arXiv API failed.

assessment.claim: 2: pi phase jumps at nu=-1/2 from e/2 encircling one more localized e/2
assessment.note: Willett et al. reported predominantly pi phase flips in FPI interference at 5/2 in GaAs; question and method match, the system and the antidot-selected occupancy are new.

assessment.claim: 3: pi/2 phase jumps at nu=-1/2 attributed to e/2 encircling a localized e/4, expected non-Abelian
assessment.note: Willett et al. claimed interference evidence of non-Abelian e/4 and Abelian e/2 braiding at 5/2 in GaAs; the paper's new element is a time-resolved pi/2 jump of the e/2 pattern in bilayer graphene. Not cited.

assessment.claim: Explicit priority statement (p. 6): sharply defined aperiodic jumps at nu=-1/2 have not been reported before
assessment.note: True for the bilayer graphene nu=-1/2 state (Ref. 18 saw no individual phase slips there), but pi phase flips at the analogous 5/2 state in GaAs were reported by Willett et al.; the wording should name that work.

assessment.claim: 4: time-resolved switching between anyon occupancies, single anyon tunnelling events
assessment.note: Telegraph switching of localized anyon number was already resolved at 1/3 in graphene interferometers (Refs. 12, 13, cited); new here is resolving it at even-denominator filling and with antidot control.

positioning: The paper extends graphene Fabry-Perot interferometry at 1/3 (Refs. 12, 13, telegraph noise and slow anyon dynamics) and the group's own even-denominator AB interference (Ref. 18, arXiv:2412.19886) by adding an antidot that sets which localized anyon type sits in the loop, giving resolved pi and pi/2 jumps at nu=-1/2; the closest GaAs precedent for e/2 and e/4 braiding signatures at 5/2 (Willett et al., arXiv:1905.10248 and 0911.0345) is not cited, and a concurrent graphene antidot experiment (arXiv:2603.11182, Henzinger et al.) appeared the same day. The arXiv API returned HTTP 429 on every call, so coverage is the reference list plus five web searches; no claim is graded no_precedent_found for that reason. One should-address item: position the work against Willett et al.

issues.claim: Phase jumps at nu=-1/2 from braiding e/2 around localized e/2 or e/4 anyons
issues.headline: Uncited GaAs 5/2 interferometry already reported e/4 and e/2 braiding
issues.issue: Willett et al. (arXiv:1905.10248, and earlier arXiv:0911.0345) reported Fabry-Perot interference at 5/2 in GaAs attributed to non-Abelian e/4 and Abelian e/2 braiding, with predominantly pi phase flips from fermion parity changes. The paper does not cite this work, yet states that sharp aperiodic jumps at half filling have not been reported before. A referee who knows the 5/2 literature will ask how these results relate.

evidence.quote: In contrast, the aperiodic jumps are sharply defined and, in the case of ν = −1/2, have not been reported before.

issues.fix: Cite Willett et al. in the introduction where earlier even-denominator interference is reviewed, and scope the priority sentence to bilayer graphene and to jumps resolved in time with a controlled antidot occupancy, stating what the antidot adds over the GaAs observations.

edit.before: In contrast, the aperiodic jumps are sharply defined and, in the case of ν = −1/2, have not been reported before.
edit.after: In contrast, the aperiodic jumps are sharply defined; at ν = −1/2 in bilayer graphene they have not been reported before, while related π phase flips at ν = 5/2 in GaAs were attributed to fermion-parity changes [Willett et al.].
